description: We are a two-member team, both holding MSc degrees in Data Science from SUST, Bangladesh. Our skills include Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Statistical Analysis, Data Visualization, and problem-solving. We are passionate about applying AI and Data Science to real-world challenges, especially Earth observation and environmental sustainability. We welcome collaboration with participants skilled in GIS, satellite data processing, software development, and UI/UX design.
summary:
EarthPulse AI is an interactive climate trend analysis platform that investigates whether Sylhet, Bangladesh, is warming uniformly throughout the year or experiencing different warming patterns across individual months and seasons.

Using NASA POWER monthly 2-meter air temperature (T2M) data from 2001 to 2025, the platform analyzes long-term temperature trends, monthly anomalies, and seasonal variations. It applies statistical methods, including the Mann-Kendall trend test and Sen's slope estimation, to help identify patterns that annual averages alone may hide.

The project aims to make climate data more understandable and accessible through interactive visualizations and an evidence-based analytical dashboard. Its findings can support climate awareness and further local climate investigations. The analysis represents a NASA POWER model grid-cell estimate near Sylhet, not direct weather-station measurements or district-wide observations.
details:
We developed EarthPulse AI to explore a question that a single annual temperature average cannot fully answer: Is Sylhet warming uniformly throughout the year, or are some months and seasons changing differently from others? To investigate this, we used NASA POWER monthly Temperature at 2 Meters (T2M) data covering 2001–2025 for a representative location near Sylhet, Bangladesh. We cleaned and examined the dataset, explored temperature anomalies, compared monthly and seasonal patterns, and conducted statistical trend analysis to understand how temperature has changed over time.

What makes EarthPulse AI distinctive is our idea of a Sylhet Seasonal Climate Fingerprint—a month-by-month perspective that looks beyond annual averages to explore the temperature behaviour of different parts of the year. We organized our analysis around four seasons: winter, pre-monsoon, monsoon, and post-monsoon. Through interactive charts, visualizations, and statistical summaries, we made complex climate information easier to explore and understand. Our goal was not simply to display temperature data, but to help people discover the stories hidden within it.

We developed the project using Google Colab as our coding and experimentation environment, with Python as the primary programming language. We used Pandas and NumPy for data processing and numerical analysis, SciPy and statistical methods for trend analysis, and Matplotlib and Plotly for data visualization. We built the interactive dashboard with Streamlit, allowing users to explore temperature patterns, monthly changes, and seasonal comparisons in an accessible way.

We believe understanding climate change begins with asking better local questions. EarthPulse AI aims to support climate awareness, education, and further investigation by making NASA climate data more accessible and meaningful. Our analysis uses a single NASA POWER MERRA-2 model grid-cell estimate near Sylhet, rather than direct weather-station measurements or district-wide observations. Therefore, the findings are exploratory and should be interpreted within this limitation. Ultimately, we want to encourage people to look beyond a single average and discover how the climate story may differ from one month to another.
